papers.title: LaST-R1: Reinforcing Action via Adaptive Physical Latent Reasoning for VLA Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have increasingly incorporated reasoning mechanisms for complex robotic manipulation. We present LaST-R1, a unified VLA framework that integrates latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning over physical dynamics prior to action execution, along with a tailored RL post-training paradigm. We propose Latent-to-Action Policy Optimization (LAPO), a novel RL algorithm that jointly optimizes the latent reasoning process and the action generation. Extensive experiments show that LaST-R1 achieves a near-perfect 99.8% average success rate on the LIBERO benchmark with only one-shot supervised warm-up.

papers.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy
papers.abstract: Octo is a transformer-based robot policy trained on 800k robot trajectories from the Open X-Embodiment dataset. It can be finetuned to adapt to new robot embodiments, tasks, and sensory inputs. Octo represents a step towards generalist robot policies that can be shared and adapted across the robotics community.

papers.title: RL-VLA: Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: We introduce RL-VLA, a framework for fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action models using reinforcement learning from environment feedback. Unlike supervised approaches that only imitate demonstrations, RL-VLA enables VLAs to explore and learn from trial and error, significantly improving performance on complex manipulation tasks.

papers.title: GR-2: A Generative Robot Language Model for Grounded Language Understanding
papers.abstract: GR-2 is a generative model that predicts future video frames conditioned on robot actions and language instructions. By learning visual dynamics in a video prediction framework, GR-2 acquires a rich understanding of physical interactions that can be applied to robot control across diverse embodiments and tasks.

papers.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
papers.abstract: Diffusion Policy introduces a novel approach to visuomotor policy learning by formulating action generation as a denoising diffusion process. It generates action sequences conditioned on visual observations, demonstrating strong performance on complex manipulation tasks requiring high-frequency precision and multi-modal action distributions.
